Resolves #20987

Screen 1 keeps two controls. "Get started" stays. The second button now reads **"Who it's for"**, with an arrow-down icon on its right, in place of "View on GitHub", and it scrolls to the audience doors through `MainContainer#scrollToPart('home-audience-doors')`. Activating it moves focus to the doors' header, so a keyboard visitor continues there. The header keeps GitHub. This is the operator's selection of 21 Nov ([record](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/20987#issuecomment-7069509341)), delegated in [the reopening](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/20987#issuecomment-7069565270).

Screen 1 also fits a short snapping screen now. On `dev` the hero stood 16.5 px taller than the screen at 900 × 700. The short-screen block reviewed on #21814 joins, as the home's design seat chose ([fork (a)](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/21832#issuecomment-7069945387)).

Evidence: L3 (headless Chromium in the e2e runner: frames of the dev-served Portal, `dev` against this branch; e2e red on `dev` sources and on a no-op focus diagonal, green here; the scroller check red on `dev` at 900 × 700, green here; a blind two-reader cold read) → L3 required (AC-2 behaviour, AC-3 pair and cold read). Residual: none.

## Deltas from ticket

- The class `.neo-github` becomes `.hero-audience-cue`, both in `hero/Content.css` (the button variables) and in `HeaderToolbar.css`. The second file holds the hero buttons' entrance animation (`show-github-button` → `show-audience-cue`); without it the cue would skip its fade-in.
- The keyboard spec asserts the focus move itself. The cue is now the hero's last control, so Tab reaches the doors by DOM order alone: with a no-op `focusHeader()`, "the next Tab stays inside the doors" still passes. The `toBeFocused()` check is what fails there.
- The arrow is the Button's own icon (`iconCls: 'fa fa-arrow-down'`, `iconPosition: 'right'`), as the operator suggested during review, rather than a "↓" in the label. It draws the same on every platform and joins the header's icon set. Font Awesome 7.3.1 gives the glyph empty alt text (`content: var(--fa)/""`), so the accessible name reads "Who it's for".
- The doors' two scroll buttons, "Explore the Engine" and "Explore the Agent OS", take the same icon. They sit one screen below the cue, and Clio asked for them with this change so that a visitor does not see the icon and the typed glyph within one scroll ([frame](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/60d3b5f83535a69b4dc3ecb3a8200665c374470d/proof/20987-second-button/icon-doors-dark-1440x900.jpg?raw=true)).
- The other seven typed arrows from Clio's defect note go too, on the operator's direction of 22 Nov ("there is no until after the cut. NOW."):
  - On the doors, the three proof links take an icon element beside their text, and "Read What Is Neo.mjs?" takes the Button's icon ([frame](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/e516e52bd628bc8c24fc5f4c09b1da437d6650b2/proof/20987-second-button/allicons-doors-all-dark-1440x900.jpg?raw=true)).
  - On the examples page, the cards' "Open live" cue and the tiles' cue take `fa-arrow-up-right-from-square`, and "or the Workstation" takes `fa-arrow-right` ([overview](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/e516e52bd628bc8c24fc5f4c09b1da437d6650b2/proof/20987-second-button/allicons-examples-overview-dark-1440x900.jpg?raw=true), [tiles](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/e516e52bd628bc8c24fc5f4c09b1da437d6650b2/proof/20987-second-button/allicons-examples-tiles-dark-1440x900.jpg?raw=true)).
  - The cue anchor is `aria-hidden`, and the proof icons are `aria-hidden` too.
  - The proof icons draw inline (`--fa-display: inline`). Font Awesome's default inline-block let the Study proof's arrow start a line by itself at 390 × 844, as Sophie found. Inline, the icon stays after the label's last word, at 390 and at 320 where two labels wrap. The doors' mobile layout test now checks it: red with inline-block, green here.
- The short-screen block and the scroller check from `ada/20987-screen1-cue` join, by Clio's fork (a). The restated criteria had dropped them with the door row, but the measurement showed they repair Screen 1 itself. The block sets gap 1.75rem and padding 3em 2em at min-width 841px and max-height 820px; 1440 × 900 sits outside that query.

Frame critique:
- **The hero loses its labelled path to the repository.** This is the cost the ticket named. Reader 2 said the GitHub button made `dev` "read more clearly as a code project"; reader 1 noted the GitHub icon in the header. Kept as decided.
- **On the phone the replay caption meets the bottom edge**, on `dev` and here alike. Both readers took it as a hint that more follows. The phone does not snap, so no change.
- **900 × 700 overflowed by 16.5 px on `dev`**, putting the replay caption and legend on the bottom edge. Fixed here: they stand clear at 900 × 700 and 1280 × 720.

## Cold look

Two zero-context readers, one at a time. Each saw four unlabelled stills, desktop and phone of A and B, and nothing else. `dev` was the blind control, in swapped order. Each was asked whether more follows below (0–10) and what they would click first.

| Reader · theme · order | "More below?" `dev` | "More below?" branch | First click on `dev` / branch | Preferred |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 · dark · A = `dev` | 4 desktop, 6 phone: "feels self-contained and ends in a 'View on GitHub' exit" | 9 both: "a direct pointer to a section below" | Get started / Who it's for ↓ | branch |
| 2 · light · A = branch | 5: "looks like a finished poster" | 9: "the down arrow promises a next section" | Get started / Who it's for ↓ | branch |

Both readers named the cue as the low-commitment way to learn whether the site is for them before "Get started". They saw the arrow as text; the icon draws the same arrow.

**e2e probes** (local runner): on `dev` sources the four new cases fail (no cue). With `focusHeader()` as a no-op, the two scroll cases pass and the two keyboard cases fail on `toBeFocused()`. At this head, all four pass, and so does the rest of `HomeAudienceDoorsNL.spec.mjs`.

**Identity** (`neo-identity-update`, ADR 0018). ACTIONS touched: yes.
- CTA-bearing surfaces: the label's only tracked occurrence was `hero/Content.mjs` (`git grep` over the whole tree on `dev`). The header's GitHub door is unchanged.
- Door type: for first-time visitors on Screen 1, the hero's second door changes from the repository (proof and contribute, off-site) to an in-page step into the audience-segmented doors. The target is live (`home-audience-doors`, e2e above), and the proof links sit on the doors.
- No business-owned content and no out-of-tree changes.

App-work gate: read `hero/Content.mjs`, `AudienceDoors.mjs` and `MainContainer.mjs`, and loaded `src/Neo.mjs`, `src/core/Base.mjs`, `src/state/Provider.mjs`, `src/data/Model.mjs` and `src/data/Store.mjs`.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge OR documented search (per guide §7.1):**

- **Challenge**: Non-blocking markup trade-off between `.hero-audience-cue` (`hero/Content.mjs:97-102`) and `AudienceDoors`'s own in-page scroll CTAs (`AudienceDoors.mjs:147-155, 267-273, 309-323`). `AudienceDoors` binds `url: resolveSectionAnchorUrl(targetId)` (`/#<id>`) plus `DomEvents.registerPreventDefaultTargets` so the buttons render as `<a href="/#...">`, whereas `.hero-audience-cue` omits `url` and renders as a `<button>`. That avoids hash-jump prevention plumbing and preserves `#/home`, and it is safe for crawler/SSR discovery because `AudienceDoors` (`<h2>Who Neo.mjs Is For</h2>` and all three doors) is already rendered inline immediately below the hero in the same Home SSR document.
